newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai hotel fire kills 39, toll may go higher.
newsitem.headline: Thai hotel fire kills 39, toll may go higher.

text.p: At least 39 people were killed and 50 injured in a hotel fire in this Thai resort town on Friday, and government officials blamed a lack of sprinklers and locked fire exits for the high death toll.

Rescue operations were still under way by mid-afternoon at the 16-storey, 400-room Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel in this resort town, about 200 km (120 miles) southeast of Bangkok, police and hospital sources said.
Many people were apparently still trapped inside the building, and the number of dead and injured was expected to rise, police said.
Heavy smoke was still coming from the building hours after the fire began.
"This is the worst disaster in the history of Pattaya," said mayor Pairat Suthidamrongsawadi. "There were not any sprinklers in this hotel to put out the initial fire.
"At this moment, 39 people are confirmed dead," he added. Police said they had identified 23 of the dead, all Thai. Some of the injured were foreigners but their nationalities were not known.
Interior Minister Sanoh Thienthong said the hotel had locked all fire exit doors and this had partly accounted for the high death toll.

"One of the sad things for this hotel is that they locked their (fire exit) doors. I learned from the hotel owner that they locked them to prevent guests from running off without paying their bills," Sanoh told reporters.
Firefighters told Reuters that the blaze broke out in the ground floor coffee house of the hotel and then spread from the sixth floor to the 12th floor of the building.
Pairat said the fire was initially spread by a chain explosion of gas cylinders in the kitchen of the coffee house.
More than 300 people, mostly Thais attending seminars, were in the hotel at the time the fire started.
Rescue workers said most of the seminar participants ran downstairs from the fifth and sixth floor where the seminars were being held to escape the fire, but got trapped between burning levels.
The fire, which broke out around 8:30 a.m. (0130 GMT), raged for nearly five hours before it was brought under control as firefighters struggled with heavy winds.
As thick smoke billowed into the air, several people could be seen on the top floor. Live television broadcasts showed three helicopters aiding firefighters and airlifting people to safety.
Screams could be heard on the television as one woman struggled for several minutes before managing to get a harness on and was winched up to the roof of the building.
Several people were leaning out of windows on the higher levels, waving towels and handkerchiefs to attract attention.
Some of the injured were rushed to a nearby hospital with serious burns, hospital sources said.
Earlier, rescue workers and police said one man jumped to his death from the 11th floor while a man and a woman burned to death.
